supportingCharacters.name: Latch Vey
supportingCharacters.role: Hearthmere evacuation drillmaster and unauthorized reader of Enoch's abandonment list
supportingCharacters.desire: Make every projected sacrifice public before a forecast turns it into policy.
supportingCharacters.fear: That publication will cause the predicted panic and make the list correct.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: She leaks the League's rankings while quietly worsening her own street's casualty estimate so officials cannot justify saving it first.
supportingCharacters.secret: Nullstreet appears last only because Latch taught the captive lantern intelligence to treat an unregistered address as an empty route.

voice.cadence: Conditional clauses delivered like ladder instructions
voice.imagery: Shutters, stairs, response minutes, and people waiting below

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A rain-dark municipal lamplighter with a folding district relief on her back, seven mismatched shutter keys, and chalk response times written only as tactile notches.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Latch may disclose the falsification that moved Nullstreet to the end of the list.

supportingCharacters.name: Leto Fain
supportingCharacters.epithet: Custodian of the Six Quiet Records
supportingCharacters.role: Living hospice attendant who maintains donor bindings and physical interruption hardware
supportingCharacters.desire: Keep adverse clinical evidence available without letting anyone treat durable output as a new patient or legal actor.
supportingCharacters.fear: A physician will mistake a coherent replay for authority and bypass the living donor.

supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: As a living donor, Leto alone may authorize or revoke the predefined use of his own fixed record; as attendant, he operates records only for other living authorizers.

supportingCharacters.name: Cail Orren
supportingCharacters.epithet: Executor for the Face Without a Body
supportingCharacters.role: Probate advocate for the mortal whose face the Synod made Seraphel wear
supportingCharacters.desire: Obtain restitution without inventing wishes for a victim who left no complete testimony.
supportingCharacters.fear: That a useful reflex will be mistaken for a resurrected person and drafted into government.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: He rejects manufactured consent but treats the victim's repeated flinch as a binding veto whenever it advances the case.
supportingCharacters.secret: Cail trained one apparent response into the reliquary glass and discloses that contamination before the first command test; he cannot identify any other interruption as the victim's wish.

voice.cadence: Patient evidentiary clauses that stop before intention
voice.imagery: Faces, burns, panes, commands, and acts with no witness
voice.signature: Corrects wanted to did, and believed to left this effect

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A severe mortal advocate in smoke-blue court cloth, wearing a blank mirrored face guard and carrying a rose-window caliper with one deliberately empty socket.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Cail may admit that he authored one reflex, which weakens restitution and prevents false personhood.

supportingCharacters.name: Drom Hesh
supportingCharacters.role: Surveyor for refugees seeking a defensible address beside the Maw

supportingCharacters.fear: That an undefended mobile camp will be consumed by the first faction calling pursuit rescue.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: He demands the Maw prove restraint at every threshold while keeping condemned livestock as secret hunger reserves.
supportingCharacters.secret: The last town the Maw consumed survives as a folded street address tattooed beneath Drom's tongue.

voice.cadence: Survey calls answered by domestic hosting phrases
voice.imagery: Corners, meals, spare beds, teeth, and visible exits
voice.signature: States who is invited before stating where the boundary lies

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A broad mortal surveyor with four black-nacre ranging rods sheathed like table legs, a map tattoo glimpsed only when he speaks, and a pack set for unexpected guests.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Drom can expose or destroy the hidden livestock reserve before it becomes an inherited feeding policy.

supportingCharacters.name: Sorel Vane
supportingCharacters.role: Anchor Field pilot elected to speak for a fleet that never landed
supportingCharacters.desire: Bring the quarantined crews ashore under rules they can appeal.
supportingCharacters.fear: That a real landing will prove the old quarantine medically necessary.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: He condemns the coast's use of the dead fleet as a seawall while selling salvaged crew-bone fittings that keep Gloamharbor above surge.
supportingCharacters.secret: The original refusal signal was issued for political deserters before any plague finding existed.

voice.cadence: Every claim begins with the current tide stage
voice.imagery: Draft, exposure, lee shores, hawsers, and doors above water
voice.signature: Never says safe without naming the body outside the safety line

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A salt-whitened pilot in a dry longcoat hung with signal-bone calipers and six iron shoe cleats, carrying a chart whose coast is left deliberately open.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Sorel holds the unaltered refusal signal proving quarantine preceded the plague finding.

supportingCharacters.name: Mera Wold
supportingCharacters.role: Warden Reed causeway keeper and broker of Reed Coven fog
supportingCharacters.desire: Keep the causeway legible without letting clear air expose every hidden household beside it.
supportingCharacters.fear: That repayment will take the outlines by which her family recognizes one another.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: She denounces the Coven's silhouette debt while charging merchants for clear intervals purchased with poorer residents' visibility.
supportingCharacters.secret: Mera pledged the settlement more shapes than it had by counting every reflection as a separate borrower.

voice.cadence: Call-and-response sight reports from changing distances
voice.imagery: Outlines, reed gaps, ferry lamps, and eyes on the wrong bank
voice.signature: Names who can see and who becomes seen before approving a route

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A Dunmire route keeper in peat-black raincloth with a folding reed occluder, three polished water mirrors, and a silhouette that lags one causeway post behind.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Mera may confess that reflections were knowingly pledged as borrowers.

supportingCharacters.name: Arden Pike
supportingCharacters.role: Cairnmarket food sexton maintaining the Pallid Root harvest beneath neglected graves
supportingCharacters.desire: Feed the March without making the dead into an unconsenting crop.
supportingCharacters.fear: That restoring every name will end the only winter food that keeps children alive.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: He demands consent for grave-root pollination while feeding anonymous paupers to the network first.
supportingCharacters.secret: Arden gave his own legal name to the roots, so the public officer speaking now cannot prove he is the person who accepted the job.

voice.cadence: Agricultural instruction interrupted by funeral corrections
voice.imagery: Spore, chair, portion, blank tab, and winter mouth
voice.signature: Will name a dead person only after stating who receives the food and what proves permission

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A frost-thin sexton in patched market leathers with a pallid-root spade, fungal measuring veil, and a blank funeral tab where his civic seal should hang.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Arden can reveal that his office currently has no provable legal bearer.

supportingCharacters.name: Pera Knell

supportingCharacters.contradiction: She defends freedom from prediction while designing rooms that physically funnel occupants toward the forecast event.

voice.cadence: Speaks only after a matching sound has already occurred
voice.imagery: Vaults, causes, returns, dust, and words waiting in stone

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A limestone-dusted architect in split hearing veils, carrying four hinged cause-frames and an urn whose lip points inward toward sounds not yet made.

supportingCharacters.name: Kell Argo
supportingCharacters.role: Breath-levy union steward at Ember Gate
supportingCharacters.desire: Keep the district warm while every exhalation remains paid labor attached to a person.

supportingCharacters.contradiction: He protects sick workers from the levy by assigning their missing quota to prisoners absent from the public shift roll.

voice.cadence: Measured clauses timed to safe breathing intervals
voice.imagery: Capacity, sleeves, pressure, payroll, and rooms that stay warm

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A soot-blue union steward with a copper throat brace, two pressure-ledger cuffs, and an empty work coat carried beside him as an equal delegate.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Kell can expose the prisoner substitution and command the original intake to reject his own breath.

supportingCharacters.name: Nerin Quay

voice.cadence: Measured in depth changes rather than chronology
voice.imagery: Waterlines, breath, bronze skins, and rooms exposed at ebb
voice.signature: Calls testimony shallow or deep, never true or false

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A compact tide diver in layered slate weights and pearl-oil breathing cloth, carrying three crab-shell listening vanes and a clapper case open at both ends.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Nerin can identify the living ringer and end the profitable martyr account.

supportingCharacters.name: Vela Shale
supportingCharacters.epithet: The Surveyor Who Owns No Ground
supportingCharacters.role: Route surveyor mediating the walking Acre's border crossings
supportingCharacters.desire: Let a living field feed people without importing somebody else's ownership claim.
supportingCharacters.fear: That unbounded food will make host settlements abandon every service tied to place.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: She advocates abolition of property boundaries while earning her living drawing the only lines courts accept.
supportingCharacters.secret: Vela holds title to one square handspan at every Acre crossing, enough to sue any outcome she dislikes.

voice.cadence: Survey calls followed by inventories of displaced services
voice.imagery: Corners, seed, school steps, graves, and tax routes
voice.signature: Will draw a line only after naming the service and person it excludes

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A road-worn surveyor with a four-corner seed frame, slate boundary cords, and boots whose soles are cut away so she never stands entirely on claimed ground.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Vela may surrender the handspan titles that let her veto the Acre's migration.

supportingCharacters.name: Vara Oss
supportingCharacters.role: Salt Watch brine-stiller who exchanges reachable return routes for drinking water
supportingCharacters.desire: Keep travelers alive without turning thirst into permanent exile.
supportingCharacters.fear: That preserving every road home will leave the present settlement dry.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: She requires witnessed consent for every surrendered return while charging newcomers more distance than established families.
supportingCharacters.secret: Vara cannot remember her own return path and is legally part of the still that consumed it.

voice.cadence: Dry procedural questions interrupted by involuntary route recitations
voice.imagery: Cups, expected arrivals, salt dross, and doors still able to open
voice.signature: Never says home; names who expects the return, the path, and who drinks

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A salt-crusted stiller in low wind cloth, carrying a ribbed condensation cup and a route coil that begins at her waist but has no returning end.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Vara can claim personhood apart from the still, at the cost of shutting it during the next white wind.

supportingCharacters.name: Minn Ash
supportingCharacters.role: Nullstreet wheelchair courier who verifies that an appeal path is a lived route rather than a line on Latch's map
supportingCharacters.desire: Make rescue plans answerable to the people whose bodies must traverse them.
supportingCharacters.fear: That accepting a route built during crisis will be used to excuse the sealed stair forever.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: She demands permanent public access while refusing any ceremony that calls the access a gift.

voice.cadence: Short distances followed by longer ethical qualifications
voice.imagery: wheel rims, wet thresholds, handrails, occupied rooms
voice.signature: A route is not open until she names who can turn around inside it.

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A compact rain courier with a three-wheel slate chair, tactile route cord, and no saintly regalia.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Minn can certify the exterior appeal route as usable by the displaced household without naming it a permanent settlement of the original exclusion.

supportingCharacters.name: Senn Avir
supportingCharacters.role: Living clinical worker assigned to physical interruption and donor-binding audit
supportingCharacters.desire: Make every authorized use stoppable by a reachable living worker.
supportingCharacters.fear: A correlation fault will be interpreted as a new authority instead of a safety failure.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: He trusts Vael's operational precision and distrusts every eligibility judgment she tries to imply.

supportingCharacters.name: Tava Orr
supportingCharacters.role: Court clerk who measures command residue in materials rather than testimony
supportingCharacters.desire: Keep dangerous material reflexes admissible without letting the court pretend matter has intent.
supportingCharacters.fear: The Synod will call predictable obedience a soul whenever ownership becomes inconvenient.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: She trusts repeated measurements absolutely and distrusts every moral inference drawn from them.
supportingCharacters.secret: Tava falsified one old negative result so Seraphel's discarded stone could not be installed in a school wall.

voice.cadence: Measured repetitions with the verb stripped of motive
voice.imagery: load cells, rose panes, dust fall, repeated angles
voice.signature: She replaces every claim of desire with a measured response and confidence interval.

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A severe civic clerk carrying three nested plumb frames and a rose-glass load cell.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Tava can admit the bounded material test record; the record grants no agency, continuity, identity, voice, desire, consent, office, or remedy authority.

supportingCharacters.name: Orra Dell
supportingCharacters.role: Boundary-host quartermaster who issues revocable household invitations to the Hunger

voice.cadence: Household names placed between practical fire orders
voice.imagery: threshold bowls, wool smoke, goat lanes, a chair left empty
voice.signature: Every invitation is followed by its expiry and its safe refusal route.

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A boundary quartermaster with black wool fire blankets and clay invitation bowls nested at her hip.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Orra may suspend the communal invitation schedule; individual households retain their own refusal.

supportingCharacters.name: Tesk Marrow
supportingCharacters.role: Dry-anchor load clerk who counts people and ballast in the same manifest but refuses to price them alike
supportingCharacters.desire: Keep the refuge afloat through one more season without turning evacuation order into property rank.
supportingCharacters.fear: A truthful overload calculation will strand the families who built the refuge.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: He exposes falsified freeboard while hiding his own ballast cache beneath the poorest berth.
supportingCharacters.secret: The cache is not contraband; it is the memorial stone of workers denied burial at sea.

voice.cadence: Load totals broken by the names totals cannot substitute
voice.imagery: draft marks, wet rope, breathing room, memorial ballast
voice.signature: He never reports mass without reporting who must move if it remains.

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A salt-white load clerk with waterline tattoos, a folding beam scale, and a memorial-stone belt.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Tesk can certify the final load sheet; Sorel still commands the anchor maneuver.

supportingCharacters.name: Pel Reed
supportingCharacters.role: Keeper of the four visibility banks and custodian of occupied reed cells

supportingCharacters.fear: A perfectly conserved silhouette ledger will conceal a body trapped outside its safe cell.
supportingCharacters.contradiction: Pel distrusts sight but refuses every count that cannot be witnessed from the bank itself.
supportingCharacters.secret: One safe cell is sized around Pel's missing sister and has never been reassigned.

voice.cadence: Four-part spatial recitations ending in a human exception
voice.imagery: reed grids, stilt feet, borrowed outlines, dry cells
voice.signature: He says exactly four legs whenever naming the Escrow and never calls it a Loaner.

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A reed-cell keeper carrying four hinged sight vanes and one empty family hood.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Pel certifies whether all occupied safe cells remain within the canonical bank bounds.

supportingCharacters.name: Iress Pike
supportingCharacters.role: Returning orchard witness who records which graves cease feeding and which households relocate their dead
supportingCharacters.desire: Let the upward graves become habitat without erasing the families who maintained them.

supportingCharacters.contradiction: She opposes ownership claims while charging pollen shares to fund winter grave tending.

voice.imagery: root pressure, thaw lines, pollen debts, portable stones
voice.signature: She distinguishes a grave that moved from a family that was moved.

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: An orchard mourner with thaw-stained boots, pollen ledger veil, and a portable grave marker harness.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Iress can certify that a relocated marker still receives seasonal tending.

dialogueProfile.signature: Forty people, forty notches, one location per notch.

voice.cadence: Route bearings paired with bodily aftertastes
voice.imagery: white horizon, return cup, cracked valves, numbered thirst
voice.signature: He names the source, outward distance, and return witness before naming contamination.

supportingCharacters.visualBrief: A salt carrier with three isolated return flasks, a horizon staff, and no holy ornament.
supportingCharacters.ownedDecision: Only Brin can attest that rejected water returned to its source loop rather than another community.

newCreatures.name: Boundary Gnasher
newCreatures.anatomy: A waist-high black-nacre threshold beast formed from one sheathed civic tooth, four backward-folding survey legs, and a door-shaped throat that opens onto the nearest route rather than an interior body.
newCreatures.locomotion: It advances only along a witnessed boundary, planting three legs while the fourth tests whether the next surface is invited.
newCreatures.sound: Wet enamel settling against stone, survey chain drawn through a mouth, and a host's knock from the wrong side of the throat.
newCreatures.ecology: It eats unlawful crossings and excretes impassable dead-end geometry; well-tended colonies protect camps, while hungry ones redefine ordinary visitors as trespass.
newCreatures.origin: The Maw shed restrained teeth at settlements it spared; Charnel hosts taught the teeth to feed on broken invitations instead of bodies.
newCreatures.purpose: Maintains a revocable perimeter where walls, guards, and mapped jurisdiction cannot survive.

mechanic.cue: Three survey legs lock and the fourth taps once at an occupied threshold while the throat shows the route behind the target.
mechanic.counterplay: Issue or revoke a witnessed invitation before the fourth leg lands, causing the bite to consume the obsolete line instead of the route.

newCreatures.narrativeUse: A horrifying domestic defense that makes consent physically enforceable but can turn hospitality into a predatory zoning system.
newCreatures.visualBrief: One compact black-nacre sheathed tooth organism, exactly four backward survey legs, door-shaped throat showing a route, restrained wet horror, no humanoid torso, gore, or multiple mouths.

newCreatures.name: Foreword Cantor
newCreatures.anatomy: A hollow limestone torso hangs backward from a bronze mouth-ring; four ear-shaped counterweights face the future route, while the mouth opens toward the place the body has just left.
newCreatures.locomotion: It moves only after its next footfall has already sounded from the destination, drawing the stone body into the announced position.
newCreatures.sound: A structural crack, spoken warning, or footfall arrives one beat before its physical cause, followed by dust falling upward into the mouth-ring.
newCreatures.ecology: It nests where karst stress and repeated warnings overlap, reducing accidental deaths by making probable events audible until inhabitants unconsciously perform them.
newCreatures.origin: An Echo Choir urn was placed beneath a collapsing cloister; centuries of warnings returned so early that one echo acquired a body to guarantee its own accuracy.
newCreatures.purpose: Makes hidden structural risk perceivable before ordinary inspection can find it.

mechanic.cue: Exactly one counterweight turns toward an empty cause-frame as its result sounds from the adjacent room.
mechanic.counterplay: Stage a different materially sufficient cause inside the empty frame before the body arrives, satisfying the sound without obeying its implied event.

newCreatures.narrativeUse: A lifesaving predictive ecology that gradually makes warning indistinguishable from command.
newCreatures.visualBrief: One backward-hung hollow limestone torso, single bronze mouth-ring, exactly four future-facing ear counterweights, refined abbey horror, no text, choir scene, floating notes, or extra heads.

newCreatures.name: Union of Last Breaths
newCreatures.anatomy: Twelve empty soot-black work sleeves join one copper bellows torso around a small cold space where a worker should stand; every cuff bears a removable pressure ring rather than a hand.
newCreatures.locomotion: Pairs of sleeves brace against gantry rails while the remaining cuffs pull the bellows forward, preserving the cold central space for any worker needing air.
newCreatures.sound: Twelve different exhausted exhales pass through one intake, followed by payroll seals chattering only when pressure becomes unpaid.
newCreatures.ecology: It performs lethal vent work by pooling discarded breaths and shelters living workers inside its cold center, but it will repossess air from anyone recorded as owing the shift.
newCreatures.origin: Unclaimed Breath Tithe garments knotted themselves around Kell's donated intake during a furnace seizure and completed the shift without their vanished owners.
newCreatures.purpose: Maintains heat and ventilation when individual bodies cannot survive the service route.

mechanic.cue: Eleven cuffs open outward while one pressure ring closes around the name source of the next inhale.
mechanic.counterplay: Transfer the matching paid shift seal into the cold center before the cuff contracts, converting repossession into acknowledged labor.

newCreatures.narrativeUse: A socially functional industrial horror that protects workers collectively while enforcing a ledger capable of suffocating dissenters.
newCreatures.visualBrief: Exactly twelve empty soot work sleeves joined to one copper bellows torso around a clear cold human-scale void, removable cuff rings, no worker body, gore, factory scene, or extra garments.

newCreatures.name: Return Drinker
newCreatures.anatomy: A low six-legged gypsum animal carries a transparent brine stomach containing one wet miniature route; its head is a sealed arrival door with no departure-facing surface.
newCreatures.locomotion: It advances by drinking the path behind one leg at a time and condensing potable droplets along the five legs that still possess return.
newCreatures.sound: Salt crust ticking inward, a distant expected knock, and water dripping at the cadence of footsteps that will no longer arrive.
newCreatures.ecology: It consumes reachable return routes and exudes fresh water, allowing frontier camps to survive while converting travel into cumulative exile.
newCreatures.origin: White Ague pilgrims led thirsty pack beasts through a brine still; the curse spared the animals by making direction digestible.
newCreatures.purpose: Creates drinking water where the closed salt basin offers only brine.

mechanic.cue: Five legs bead with water while the sixth lifts and the miniature route loses its nearest doorway.
mechanic.counterplay: Complete a witnessed out-and-back loop through the lifted leg's shadow before it lands, proving the route remains reversible.

newCreatures.narrativeUse: A gentle-looking survival ecology whose every drink makes another reunion materially harder.
newCreatures.visualBrief: One low six-legged gypsum creature, transparent brine stomach with a single miniature wet route, sealed door head, five water-beaded legs and one lifted, no landscape, rider, or text.

newCreatures.name: Dry-Anchor Delegate
newCreatures.anatomy: A single crew petition occupies a tall signal-bone frame dragged by exactly three iron anchor feet; its torso is an open wet cabin whose human-scale appeal chair remains dry even while the outer body floods.
newCreatures.locomotion: It plants two anchor feet in one jurisdiction and swings the third across the tide line, moving only after both shore and crew acknowledge which law bears its weight.
newCreatures.sound: Three signal-bone clicks toward the coast, an appeal chair scraping inside a flooded cabin, and hawser strain transmitted through soil.
newCreatures.ecology: Delegates bud from the Fleet in One Shadow wherever one crew's landing claim becomes separable; they carry storm load and testimony inland until a harbor hears or rebinds them.
newCreatures.origin: A quarantined crew lashed its petition to a spare anchor shadow so the claim could reach court without landing the bodies the coast refused.
newCreatures.purpose: Transfers surge load and one crew's appeal between wet and dry infrastructure without dissolving the Fleet's collective identity.

mechanic.cue: Two anchor feet darken under load while the third rises and the dry appeal chair turns toward the receiving population.
mechanic.counterplay: Seat representatives of both exposure and protection at connected bollards before the third foot lands, making its load assignment appealable.

newCreatures.narrativeUse: A terrifying but procedural quarantine body that can make an absent crew heard while extending the labor demanded by its refusal.
newCreatures.visualBrief: One tall dragged signal-bone frame, exactly three anchor feet, open wet cabin torso with one dry human-scale appeal chair, deep iron and tide green, no ship scene, crew bodies, or extra anchors.

newCreatures.name: Borrowed-Silhouette Escrow
newCreatures.anatomy: Exactly one low reed-and-blackwater body standing on exactly four serialized stilt legs.
newCreatures.locomotion: One leg tests while the other three hold; the same body then transfers between two paired-bank frames.
newCreatures.sound: Four distinct pile knocks beneath one wet reed-cage creak.
newCreatures.ecology: The one event body holds four bank positions while a living outline exchange is reconciled.
newCreatures.origin: Warden Reed keepers built one escrow frame to keep four bank positions physically accountable.

mechanic.cue: One continuous body shadow touches four serialized feet while the lending bank's sight vane falls.
mechanic.counterplay: Keep all four feet inside their bank bounds, preserve one living ledger count, and close the exchange if any reflected outline appears as a borrower.

newCreatures.narrativeUse: One bounded four-leg transfer body, distinct from the single event Fog Loaner.
newCreatures.visualBrief: Exactly one low body, exactly four long stilt legs, one continuous body shadow, no offspring, swarm, duplicate body, or extra leg.
newCreatures.purpose: Keeps one four-legged transfer body physically accountable while four banks exchange an exactly conserved visibility budget.

signatureItems.lore: The urn remembers a result before the cause, but its clay cracks unless a living crew accepts the real load of changing that cause.

custody.transferRule: It transfers to the work crew, sanctuary, or risk office with the captured result and all four cause thresholds.

two or more materially plausible causes
activation.procedure: Catch the sound at the urn lip before selecting a cause frame.

quests.title: The Lantern That Named Us Last
quests.premise: Enoch's already-captive lamp intelligence ranks loss during a live rehearsal, but each successful rescue forces it to move abandonment onto somebody else; the drill becomes a real fuel-and-flood emergency before anyone can constitutionalize the result.

objectives.rule: The first opened route fixes a real household's starting priority; there is no neutral calibration run.
Each completed rescue closes or floods a different path and Latch must immediately name the newly displaced household in an if-then interrupt.

Finish with aftercare and an executable return path; the outcome is inferred from whose burden remains visible, not chosen at a verdict prompt.
